extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, field observers, miners, metallurgists, and experimentalists (readers of the Royal Society seeking guidance on reporting mines, ores, metallurgy, and transfusion experiments)
extracted.subtask_description: A field- and laboratory-oriented checklist for documenting mines, ores, metallurgical practice, and an experimental surgical procedure (blood transfusion). Guides what to observe, measure, and report about geology, mine structure, ore character, smelting/reduction, and practical experimental conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rivers, brooks, springs and other waters — nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The rivers, brooks, springs, and other waters; and the nature of them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the character of local waters (flowing or stagnant), their taste, smell, ponderousness, and any indicia they give of minerals; note colors of stones and pebbles in brooks/springs and any subterraneous streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local atmosphere and weather characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the air be dry or moist, hot or cold, clear or foggy, thick or thin, heavy or light; any subterraneous streams, and what they are?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report climate and atmospheric peculiarities (dry/moist, temperature, visibility, density), unusual meteorological phenomena (thunder, lightning, storms, nocturnal lights, fiery meteors), and signs from mists or 'virgula divinatoria' that may relate to mineral occurrences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil description
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the soil be stony; and, if it be, what kind of stones it abounds with? Whether it be clayey, marly, chalky, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail soil texture and composition, identify dominant rock fragments or earth types, and describe how these relate to local mineralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs or indications of mines (surface vegetation and damage)
rubrics_metrics.description: By what signs they know or guess that there is a mine in such a place? Whether it be observed that trees and other greater plants seem to have their tops burned, or other leaves or outsides discoloured? Or whether there be any plants that affect to grow over such mines, or the contrary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note any abnormal plant coloration, stunted or burned-appearing crowns, or specific species preferring mineralized ground as indicators of subsurface ore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water-borne indicators of minerals
rubrics_metrics.description: What colour the stones and pebbles take in the brooks, springs, or other waters?— Whether the waters, by their taste, smell, ponderousness, &c. indicate any minerals?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe discoloration in streambed sediments, unusual taste/odor/weight of water, precipitates or residues that suggest dissolved minerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal and microclimatic signs (snow, frost, dew)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether snow will not lie, or frost continue so long, or dew be collected upon the ground, more or less than usual? — And whether the dew or the rain there will discolour white linen or woollen cloths, spread over night on the surface of the ground?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record anomalies in freezing, thawing, or dew deposition and any staining of fabric by dew/rain that might indicate mineral salts or other substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geophysical and meteorological hazards or phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: The state of the place as to thunder and lightning, storms or earthquakes, nocturnal lights and fiery meteors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document frequency and character of storms, seismicity, and luminous phenomena which may correlate with geology or subsurface features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface geomorphological indicators for vein tracing
rubrics_metrics.description: What signs afford a probability of mines, or direction for following a vein over hills, valleys, lakes, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide surface clues (outcrops, aligned discolored soils, linear vegetational changes) useful for projecting vein direction across varied terrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsurface strata description
rubrics_metrics.description: The strata under the surface: their number, nature, depth, order, thickness, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe stratigraphic sequence, layer thicknesses, depth and order of beds, and any peculiar earths or signature minerals; include observations of marcasites or indicative stones and presence of subterranean heat or damp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaft and grove dimensions and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth of the shaft or grove: what its width and extent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exact measurements (depth, width, lateral extent) of shafts, groves and access ways used to reach the vein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vein orientation, inclination and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the vein run horizontal or dip? what inclination it has? What its flexures; and what its directions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record strike and dip, curvature/flexure patterns, and directional trends of the vein to aid mapping and follow-up work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-shafts and ventilation configuration
rubrics_metrics.description: What air-shaft belongs to the mine? Whether it be single, double, &c. and if several, what their distances, situation, &c.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe number, placement, spacing and design of air-shafts; note their effectiveness for ventilation and relation to working galleries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater ingress and drainage in mines
rubrics_metrics.description: What waters spring in the mine; at what depths; and their quantity and nature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document depth of water inflows, flow rates or volume, water chemistry/nature, and seasonal variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dewatering methods and engines
rubrics_metrics.description: What expedients and engines are employed to free the mines from water?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report pumping mechanisms, drainage adits, waterwheels, or other engineering solutions, their operation schedule and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adit conditions and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the conditions, number, &c. of the adits?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerate adits, their dimensions, gradient, and role in ventilation/drainage and ore access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damps and underground gases
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the mine be troubled with damps, and of what kind they are?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note presence of foul air, inflammable gases or other 'damps', their locations, suspected composition, and any mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for following and tracing veins underground
rubrics_metrics.description: What methods the mine men use in following the vein and tracing their passages under ground (which they call plumming and dyalling) according to the several exigencies?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe surveying and alignment techniques used underground (plumbing/dialling), instruments, procedures and adaptations for different conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of magnetic instruments and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: And whether they employ the instruments made with the help of the loadstone, the same way that is usual, or what other instruments? — What methods they take to secure themselves from the uncertainty incident to the guidance of magnetic needles from the iron-stone ore that they may meet with under ground?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether compasses/loadstone instruments are used, how magnetic anomalies from iron ores are detected/compensated, and alternative orientation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rock and spar management before reaching ore
rubrics_metrics.description: How the miners deal with the rocks and spars they often meet with before they come at the ore? Whether they use fire to soften, calcine, or crack them? How they employ it, and with what measure of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mechanical or thermal methods (fire-setting, heating/cooling) to break hostile rock types, procedures, and observed success rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruments for breaking rock and mining practice
rubrics_metrics.description: What instruments they use to break the rock, &c.? And how the mine men work; whether naked or clothed? And what lights they use to work by?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List hand and mechanical tools, safety and clothing practices, illumination types (lamps, candles), and working ergonomics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vein loss and recovery practices; teamwork on veins
rubrics_metrics.description: How veins are followed, lost, and recovered? And how several miners work on the same vein? And what is the best way of getting all the ore in a vein and most conveniently?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe techniques for regaining lost alignment, coordination among miners sharing a vein, sequencing of extraction to maximize yield and convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ore transport out of the mine
rubrics_metrics.description: How they convey out their ore and other things that are to be carried out of the mine?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report haulage systems (sledges, skips, baskets, animals, waterways), capacities, and logistical arrangements for moving ore to surface or processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and distribution of the ore (mode of occurrence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the ore runs in the vein, or lies dispersed in scattered pieces; or be divided partly into a vein, and partly into loose masses; or like a wall between two rocks, as it were in a cleft; or be interspersed in the firm rock, like speckled marble? Or be found in grains like sand or gravel; or whether the ore be of a softer consistence, like earth or lome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize the ore's mode of occurrence (lodes, pockets, disseminated, alluvial grains, earthy ores), and relate to mining technique implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical properties of ore (weight, colour, mixture)
rubrics_metrics.description: And what is observable in it as to weight, colour, mixture, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record specific gravity/weight, color, grain size, textural relations and any visible associations with gangue minerals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of native metal and plant-like growths
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether any part of the metal be found in the mine perfect and complete? Whether the mine affords any parcels of metal that seem to grow like plants, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note occurrences of native (free) metal, crystalline/filamentous growth forms that appear 'growing' from matrix, and specimens of unusually large grains or lumps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vein depth, coats and extraneous substances
rubrics_metrics.description: The depth of the vein. Its concomitants or coat. — What are the principal qualities of these extraneous substances: as that spar is white, but transparent, almost like coarse crystal, heavy, brittle, easily divisible into flakes, &c?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe depth to ore horizon, nature of vein selvage or 'coat', and detailed physical/optical/mechanical properties of associated gangue (cleavage, transparency, brittleness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vein continuity and interruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the vein be inclosed every way in its coats; or whether it only lie between them? — Whether the vein be uninterrupted, or in some places broken off; and whether it be abruptly or not; and whether it be by vales, brooks, gullets, &c.? — How wide the interruptions are; what signs whereby to find the vein again?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report continuity of the lode, presence/width of faults or pinch-outs, and surface/subsurface markers helpful to relocate interrupted segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ore grade and yield proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: What proportion of metal it affords? as in our iron mines it is observed, that about three tuns of iron-stone will afford one tun of metal: and I have had lead ore... to afford three parts in four of good lead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative yield measurements (ore-to-metal ratios, empirical smelting results) from assays or smelting trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metallurgical composition and metal associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the ore be pure in its kind from other metals? and if not, of what metals it participates; and in what proportion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe multi-metallic associations (e.g., lead with silver, iron with gold), relative proportions observed, and examples from local assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanic and preparatory operations for reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the mechanic and previous operations, as beating, grinding, washing, &c. that are used to separate the ore from the heterogeneous bodies, and prepare it for the fire?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail pre-smelting beneficiation methods (crushing, grinding, washing, concentration) and how they are practiced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mercury/amalgamation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mercury be made use of, to extract the nobler from the baser metals?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether amalgamation is used to concentrate precious metals, descriptions of the process and observed effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burning and beating as ore preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the burning and beating of the ore be used to prepare it for the furnace?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe roasting, calcining, or mechanical treatments used prior to smelting and their intended effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluxes, trial assays and quality tests
rubrics_metrics.description: What flux-powders, and other ways they have to try and examine the goodness of the ore in small quantities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List flux materials, small-scale assaying techniques, cupellation or other quick tests used to estimate ore quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smelting modes: flux vs. direct fire
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, when they work in great, they use to melt the ore with any flux or additaments, or only by the force of the fire, or in any way between both?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether flux-assisted smelting or raw roasting is employed at industrial scale and rationale for chosen method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnace types and fuel usage
rubrics_metrics.description: What kind of furnaces they use to melt the ore in? — What kinds of fuel, and what quantities of it, are wont to be employed in the furnace, within the compass of a day or week? How much is put in at a time? How often it is renewed? and how much ore in a determinate time, as a week or a day, is wont to be reduced to metal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe furnace design, fuel types and consumption rates, charging schedules, and throughput (ore reduced per unit time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of fire/blast application
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the ore be melted by a wind excited by the fire itself, as in wind ovens? Or by the course of waters? Or actuated by the blast of bellows?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the driving force for combustion (natural draft, hydraulic power, bellows/blowers) and implications for temperature control and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and moulding practices
rubrics_metrics.description: What contrivance they have to let or take out the metal that is in fusion, and cast it into bars, sows, pigs, &c. — What clay, sand, or mould they let it run or pour it through? And after what manner they refrigerate it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe tapping/casting method, mould materials and designs, cooling protocols and casting yields/defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-fusion treatment and refining
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether they do any thing to the metal after it is once brought to fusion, and if need be, melt it over again, to give it a melioration? As when iron is refined and turned into steel; and what distinct furnaces and peculiar ways of ordering the metals are employed to effect this improvement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document refining, re-melting, refining furnaces (e.g., fineries), and techniques to improve metal quality (e.g., steel production).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnace residues and 'metalline flowers'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether, in those places where the metal is melted, there be not elevated some corpuscles, that stick to the upper parts of the furnace or building? And if there be, whether they be barely fuliginous and recrementitious exhalations or at least in part, metalline flowers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and describe any condensates, soot, or metallic 'flowers' appearing in furnace architecture, and note whether they contain metal or are merely fuliginous residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recrements and secondary yields from fusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the metal, being brought to fusion, affords any recrements? — Whether, after the metal has been once melted, the remaining part of the ore being exposed to the air, will in time be impregnated, or ripened so as to afford more metal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record slag and residua behavior, and whether tailings left after smelting change over time to yield additional metal upon reprocessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed surgical/procedural method for transfusing blood between animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise method: prepare carotid artery of donor with two ligatures and quill, prepare jugular vein of recipient with running knots and quills, connect quills so blood flows from donor artery into recipient jugular, bleed recipient's other vein into dishes proportionally, then tie and close recipient when transfusion complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified sequence: isolation and ligature of vessels, secure quills/pipes tightly, align animals so quills connect without stretch, open connections to permit arterial→venous flow, monitor recipient's condition and bleeding out, tie and close veins after procedure. Use small crooked thin pipe of silver or brass as improvement over quills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical considerations to ensure successful transfusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Several circumstances necessary to be observed ... (fasten dogs at a convenient distance; observe pulse beyond the quill; clear congealed blood; bleed a great dog into a little one; prepare animals of near equal age/diet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no vessel stretching, monitor pulse beyond quill as sign of patency, clear blocked quills promptly, prefer using a larger donor into smaller recipient or multiple donors staged to avoid stoppage; match animals by age and recent feeding to approximate blood temperament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design considerations for transfusion trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations: (1) risk of donor blood mixing with any remaining recipient blood — use multiple donors to ensure clearing; (2) conjecture that exchange of blood will not alter animals' nature but worth testing; (3) probable use is to supply deficient/corrupt blood and may require repeated transfusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to confirm complete exchange (use multiple sequential donors), test hypotheses about physiological effect of exchanged blood, and explore therapeutic potential while accounting for repeated administration and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement of transfusion apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Note only, that instead of a quill a small crooked thin pipe of silver or brass ... will be much fitter than a straight pipe or quill for this operation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a slender bent metal pipe with small knob ends to better fasten to vessels, easing insertion and management over straight quills.
